verses.zh: 撒母耳对扫罗说：「耶和华差遣我膏你为王，治理他的百姓以色列；所以你当听从耶和华的话。
verses.en: Then Samuel said to Saul, “I was the one the Lord sent to anoint you as king over his people Israel. Now listen to what the Lord says.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “to the voice of the words of the Lord” (so KJV).
verses.commentary:
15:1 "The Lord" This is the covenant name for Israel's Deity from the
Hebrew verb "to be."

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "to anoint" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: "ANOINTING" IN THE BIBLE.

▣ "Israel" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (THE NAME).

▣ "the words of the Lord" This is literally the "sound" (BDB 876) of the
words (cf. 1 Sam. 12:14,15; 15:1,19,20,22). This same word is used of the sound of the sheep and cattle in v. 14.

Notice Samuel's words are in reality YHWH's words!

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华如此说：『以色列人出埃及的时候，在路上亚玛力人怎样待他们，怎样抵挡他们，我都没忘。
verses.en: Here is what the Lord of Heaven’s Armies has said: ‘I carefully observed how the Amalekites opposed[NOTE:1] Israel along the way when Israel[NOTE:2] came up from Egypt.
notes: Heb “what Amalek did to Israel, how he placed against him.”
Heb “he”; the referent (Israel) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
15:2 "the Lord of hosts" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord OF HOSTS.

▣ "Amalek for what he did to Israel" This is referring to Exod. 17:8-16; Num. 24:20; Deut. 25:17-19.
The name "Amalek" (BDB 766) or "Amalekites" does not appear outside of the OT. It may be the title for their king, like Hadad,
Pharaoh, Caesar.

verses.zh: 现在你要去击打亚玛力人，灭尽他们所有的，不可怜惜他们，将男女、孩童、吃奶的，并牛、羊、骆驼，和驴尽行杀死。』」
verses.en: So go now and strike down the Amalekites. Destroy everything they have. Don’t spare[NOTE:1] them. Put them to death—man, woman, child, infant, ox, sheep, camel, and donkey alike.’”
notes: Or perhaps “don’t take pity on” (cf. CEV).
verses.commentary:
15:3 YHWH gives several directives.

- go

- strike

- utterly destroy (lit. herem, cf. Deut. 7:26; 13:17; Josh. 6:17; 7:1,11,12,15; 22:20; 1 Chr. 2:7; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: CURSE)

- do not spare (cf. 1 Sam. 15:3,9,15; Deut. 13:8)

- put to death (i.e., holy war; no spoils, all belongs to YHWH; lit. "under the ban," cf. Lev. 27:28-29; Joshua 6; Jer. 51:3)

- man

- woman

- child

- infant

- ox

- sheep

- camel

- donkey

(If it breathes, it dies! cf. Joshua 6)

For a good brief discussion of the Herem (i.e., under the ban) see Hard Sayings of the Bible,
"Completely Destroy Them!" pp. 206-207.

verses.zh: 于是扫罗招聚百姓在提拉因，数点他们，共有步兵二十万，另有犹大人一万。
verses.en: So Saul assembled[NOTE:1] the army[NOTE:2] and mustered them at Telaim. There were 200,000 foot soldiers and 10,000 men of Judah.
notes: Heb “caused the people to hear.”
Heb “people.”
verses.commentary:
15:4 It is surprising in this period that Israel and Judah's soldiers are listed separately. This may
be an anachronism from a later editor/compiler.

▣ "Telaim" This name (BDB 378) appears only here. It is probably a variant spelling for "Telem"
(BDB 378, cf. Josh. 15:24), both of which are in Judah.

▣ "200,000. . .10,000" Remember that western literalism often forgets the eastern hyperbole
and the many connotations of the noun "thousand." A helpful book to me has been G. B. Caird, The Language
and Imagery of the Bible.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THOUSAND (eleph)

verses.zh: 扫罗到了亚玛力的京城，在谷中设下埋伏。
verses.en: Saul proceeded to the city[NOTE:1] of Amalek, where he set an ambush[NOTE:2] in the wadi.[NOTE:3]
notes: The LXX has the plural here, “cities.”

The translation follows the LXX and Vulgate which assume a reading וַיָּאָרֶב (vayyaʾarev, “and he set an ambush,” from the root אָרַב [ʾarav] with quiescence of alef) rather than the MT, which has וַיָּרֶב (vayyareb, “and he contended,” from the root רִיב [riv]).
That is, “the dry stream bed.”
verses.commentary:
15:5

NASB, TEV, NJB, NET, Vulgate
"set an ambush"

NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA, LXX
"lay in wait"

REB
"halted for a time"

Peshitta
"issued a directive"

The MT has the root ריב (BDB 936, KB 1224,

Qal IMPERFECT) which means "to contend with" or "to strive with."

The LXX suggests another root, ארב (BDB 70,

KB 83, Hiphil IMPERFECT) which means "to lie in wait" (i.e., ambush). The UBS Text Project
does not mention this possible emendation.

verses.zh: 扫罗对基尼人说：「你们离开亚玛力人下去吧，恐怕我将你们和亚玛力人一同杀灭；因为以色列人出埃及的时候，你们曾恩待他们。」于是基尼人离开亚玛力人去了。
verses.en: Saul said to the Kenites, “Go on and leave! Go down from among the Amalekites. Otherwise I will sweep you away[NOTE:1] with them. After all, you were kind to all the Israelites when they came up from Egypt.” So the Kenites withdrew from among the Amalekites.
notes: The translation follows the Syriac Peshitta and Vulgate which assume a reading אֶסְפָךְ (ʾesfak, “I sweep you away,” from the root סָפָה [safah]) rather than the MT אֹסִפְךָ (ʾosifeka, “I am gathering you,” from the root אָסַף [ʾasaf]).
verses.commentary:
15:6 "the Kenites" Notice the Qal imperatives Saul gives to them.

- go

- depart

- go down from

The reason given is their kindness (lit. hesed, cf. Gen. 21:23; 2 Sam. 3:8) to Israel
(cf. Exod. 18:9,10,19; Num. 10:29-32).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed)

▣

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NJB, REB, JPSOA, Peshitta
"Lest I destroy you"

TEV
"kill you"

LXX (BDB 62, #2)
"Lest I include you"

NET, Vulgate
"otherwise, I will sweep you away"

Most English translations follow the MT, "destroy" or "remove" (BDB 62, #4, KB 74, Qal
IMPERFECT) but the NET Bible follows the Vulgate, "sweep away" (BDB 705, KB 763, Qal
IMPERFECT).

The UBS Text Project does not mention this possible variant at all.

verses.zh: 扫罗击打亚玛力人，从哈腓拉直到埃及前的书珥，
verses.en: Then Saul struck down the Amalekites all the way from Havilah to[NOTE:1] Shur, which is next to Egypt.
notes: Heb “[as] you enter.”

verses.zh: 生擒了亚玛力王亚甲，用刀杀尽亚玛力的众民。
verses.en: He captured King Agag of the Amalekites alive, but he executed all Agag’s people[NOTE:1] with the sword.
notes: Heb “all the people.” For clarity “Agag’s” has been supplied in the translation.

verses.zh: 扫罗和百姓却怜惜亚甲，也爱惜上好的牛、羊、牛犊、羊羔，并一切美物，不肯灭绝。凡下贱瘦弱的，尽都杀了。
verses.en: However, Saul and the army spared Agag, along with the best of the flock, the cattle, the fatlings,[NOTE:1] and the lambs, as well as everything else that was of value.[NOTE:2] They were not willing to slaughter them. But they did slaughter everything that was despised[NOTE:3] and worthless.
notes: The Hebrew text is difficult here. We should probably read וְהַמַּשְׂמַנִּים (vehammasmannim, “the fat ones”) rather than the MT וְהַמִּשְׂנִים (vehammisnim, “the second ones”). However, if the MT is retained, the sense may be as the Jewish commentator Kimchi supposed: the second-born young, thought to be better than the firstlings. (For discussion see S. R. Driver, Notes on the Hebrew Text and the Topography of the Books of Samuel, 123-24.)
Heb “good.”
The MT has here the very odd form נְמִבְזָה (nemivzah), but this is apparently due to a scribal error. The translation follows instead the Niphal participle נִבְזָה (nivzah).
verses.commentary:
15:9 "the fatlings" This NOUN (BDB 1041) literally means "second born" (JPSOA). The
firstborn was to be given to YHWH as His portion, like the firstborn son (cf. Exodus 13). The NASB follows Targums and Peshitta.

The NET Bible footnote, p. 493, #15, mentions that the second born may have been considered to be
better than the firstlings (i.e, Kimchi). If so the MT should be retained (i.e., "second born").

▣

NASB, NKJV, NRSV
"despised and worthless"

TEV
"useless or worthless"

REB
"useless and of no value"

JPSOA
"cheap and worthless"

LXX
"despised and worthless artifact"

Peshitta
"vile and despised"

The LXX adds "and the best of the flocks and of the herds and of the foods and of the vineyard
and of the good things."

The MT has two Niphal PARTICIPLES.

- "despised" ‒ the MT has an unusual form (נמבזה) and is

emended to BDB 102, KB 117 (נבזה); both mean "despised,"
see NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 628-629, 2, a.

- "worthless" ‒ the meaning to this VERB (BDB 587, KB 606) is found only here. Usually the
VERB means "to dissolve" or "to melt." Possibly here it denotes livestock and food stores that are wasting,
rotting away.

verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到撒母耳说：
verses.en: Then the Lord’s message came to Samuel:

verses.zh: 「我立扫罗为王，我后悔了；因为他转去不跟从我，不遵守我的命令。」撒母耳便甚忧愁，终夜哀求耶和华。
verses.en: “I regret that I have made Saul king, for he has turned away from me and has not done what I told him to do.” Samuel became angry and he cried out to the Lord all that night.
verses.commentary:
15:11 "I regret that I made Saul king" This shocking statement is repeated in v. 35. Does YHWH "regret,"
"repent" (BDB 636, KB 688, Niphal PERFECT)? This seems to directly contradict v. 29
(BDB 636, KB 688, Niphal IMPERFECT). See G. B. Caird, The Language and Imagery
of the Bible, pp. 119-120.

Saul did not live up to his calling, anointing, and empowering. He was disobedient to YHWH's
expressed will. YHWH was "sorry" for Saul's choices and the consequences they brought on Israel.

For a good brief discussion on this issue see Hard Sayings of the Bible, "Does God
Change His Mind," pp. 108-109, and "A God Who Relents?" pp.333-334.

See how I deal with this subject in my notes from Gen. 6:6.

Gen. 6:6 "the Lord was sorry. . .He was grieved in His heart" These are anthropomorphic
phrases (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE). The first VERB
is interpreted "the Lord heaved with a sigh" (BDB 636, KB 688, Niphal
IMPERFECT with waw). The second VERB is interpreted "the
Lord was grieved into His heart" (BDB 780, KB 864, Hithpael IMPERFECT;
with waw, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE). These are intense Hebrew phrases (cf. Gen. 34:7; 45:5; 1 Sam. 2:33; 20:34;
2 Sam. 19:2; Ps. 78:40; Isa. 54:6). God is often spoken of in the Bible as being sorry or repenting (cf. Gen. 6:6-7;
Exod. 32:14; 1 Sam. 15:11; 2 Sam. 24:16; Jer. 18:7,8; 26:13,19; Jonah 3:10). However, other passages assert that
God never repents or changes His mind (cf. Num. 23:19; 1 Sam. 15:29; Jer. 4:28; Ps. 132:11). This is the tension that
always occurs when we use human terms to describe God. God is not a man, but the only words we have to describe
Him and His feelings are human terms. It must be asserted that God is not fickle. He is steadfast and longsuffering in
His redemptive purpose for humanity, but mankind's response in repentance of sin often determines God's actions in
a particular situation (cf. Ps. 106:45; Jonah).

Theologically it is God who changes, not mankind. God chooses to work with sinful humanity. His
goal is the same—a righteous people who reflect His character. This will only be accomplished by a new heart, a new
covenant (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:26-38). God chooses grace over judgment!

See
SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE (Biblical Paradoxes)).

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: PREDESTINATION VS. HUMAN FREE WILL

▣ "Samuel was distressed and cried out to the Lord" Apparently Samuel
was distressed by YHWH's reversal of His choice of Saul (cf. 1 Sam. 16:1). Samuel brought the subject
of Saul up several times in prayer. Finally, YHWH said do not pray any more about him!

verses.zh: 撒母耳清早起来，迎接扫罗。有人告诉撒母耳说：「扫罗到了迦密，在那里立了纪念碑，又转身下到吉甲。」
verses.en: Then Samuel got up early to meet Saul the next morning. But Samuel was informed, “Saul has gone to Carmel where[NOTE:1] he is setting up a monument for himself.” Then Samuel left[NOTE:2] and went down to Gilgal.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and look.”

Heb “and he turned and crossed over.” Some translations assume that the quotation continues and that “he” is Saul. The wording of the LXX, “he went down to Gilgal to Saul” assumes that Samuel is the subject and that the quotation has ended.tc The LXX also has “he returned the chariot” or “the chariot returned” before “he went down.” Again this may or may not be part of the quotation.

At the end of v. 12 the LXX and one Old Latin ms include the following words not found in the MT: “to Saul. And behold, he was offering as a burnt offering to the Lord the best of the spoils that he had brought from the Amalekites.” The Lucianic Greek translation does not include this text.
verses.commentary:
15:12 "he set up a monument for himself" The idea of a victory stele is not unusual in the ANE
but it should have been to YHWH, not Saul.

verses.zh: 撒母耳到了扫罗那里，扫罗对他说：「愿耶和华赐福与你，耶和华的命令我已遵守了。」
verses.en: When Samuel came to Saul, Saul said to him, “May the Lord bless you! I have fulfilled the Lord’s orders.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “message, word.”
verses.commentary:
15:13 Is Saul just ignorant of what YHWH said? Does he think he was obedient (v. 20)?

He gave two excuses.

- We kept these things, including Agag, alive for a sacrifice to YHWH (vv. 15,21).

- I was afraid of the soldiers revolting if they did not receive spoil v. 24).

verses.zh: 撒母耳说：「我耳中听见有羊叫、牛鸣，是从哪里来的呢？」
verses.en: Samuel replied, “If that is the case,[NOTE:1] then what is this sound of sheep in my ears and the sound of cattle that I hear?”
notes: The words “if that is the case” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 扫罗说：「这是百姓从亚玛力人那里带来的；因为他们爱惜上好的牛羊，要献与耶和华―你的　神；其余的，我们都灭尽了。」
verses.en: Saul said, “They were brought[NOTE:1] from the Amalekites; the army spared the best of the flocks and cattle to sacrifice to the Lord our God. But everything else we slaughtered.”
notes: Heb “they brought them.”
verses.commentary:
15:15 "best" This is the NOUN (BDB 406, v. 21) usually translated "the best of a thing"
(cf. here and Gen. 47:6,11 are its only uses).

There is a word play between the word "best" (vv. 15,21, BDB 406) and the ADJECTIVE
(BDB 373) in v. 28 (i.e., the new King would be better than Saul).

verses.zh: 撒母耳对扫罗说：「你住口吧！等我将耶和华昨夜向我所说的话告诉你。」扫罗说：「请讲。」
verses.en: Then Samuel said to Saul, “Wait a minute![NOTE:1] Let me tell you what the Lord said to me last night.” Saul[NOTE:2] said to him, “Tell me.”
notes: Or perhaps “be quiet.”

Heb “he”; the referent (Saul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.tc The translation follows the Qere and many medieval Hebrew mss in reading the singular (“he said”) rather than the plural (“they said”) of the Kethib.
verses.commentary:
15:16 "And he said to him" The MT has the PLURAL "they" but the Masoretic scholars
suggested a change to the SINGULAR, which is followed by most English translations.

verses.zh: 撒母耳对扫罗说：「从前你虽然以自己为小，岂不是被立为以色列支派的元首吗？耶和华膏你作以色列的王。
verses.en: Samuel said, “Is it not true that when you were insignificant in your own eyes, you became head of the tribes of Israel? The Lord chose[NOTE:1] you as king over Israel.
notes: Heb “anointed.”

verses.zh: 耶和华差遣你，吩咐你说，你去击打那些犯罪的亚玛力人，将他们灭绝净尽。
verses.en: The Lord sent you on a campaign[NOTE:1] saying, ‘Go and exterminate those sinful Amalekites! Fight against them until you[NOTE:2] have destroyed them.’
notes: Heb “journey.”
The translation follows the LXX, the Syriac Peshitta, and the Targum in reading the second person singular suffix (“you”) rather than the third person plural suffix of the MT (“they”).
verses.commentary:
15:18

NASB, NJB, JPSOA
"exterminated"

NKJV, NRSV, LXX, Peshitta
"consumed"

TEV
"killed them all"

REB
"wiped them out"

The MT has the Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 477, KB 476) of a
VERB that means "to be complete," "at an end," "finished," "accomplished." Here, it refers to the
complete slaughter of the Amalekite tribe of Agag (apparently there were other Amalekite tribes living in this location because
they appear again in later Jewish history).

This complete extermination was part of the holy war concept of an enemy being dedicated to
YHWH (i.e., under the ban, herem).

- Canaanites ‒ Deut. 7:22; Josh. 8:24; 10:20

- Amalekites ‒ 1 Sam. 15:18

- Syrians ‒ 2 Kgs. 13:17

- Assyrians ‒ Isa. 10:18

verses.zh: 你为何没有听从耶和华的命令，急忙掳掠财物，行耶和华眼中看为恶的事呢？」
verses.en: Why haven’t you obeyed[NOTE:1] the Lord? Instead you have greedily rushed upon the plunder! You have done what is wrong in the Lord’s estimation.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “listened to the voice of the Lord.”
Heb “you have done what is evil in the eyes of the Lord.”

verses.zh: 扫罗对撒母耳说：「我实在听从了耶和华的命令，行了耶和华所差遣我行的路，擒了亚玛力王亚甲来，灭尽了亚玛力人。
verses.en: Then Saul said to Samuel, “But I have obeyed[NOTE:1] the Lord! I went on the campaign[NOTE:2] the Lord sent me on. I brought back King Agag of the Amalekites after exterminating the Amalekites.
notes: Heb “listened to the voice of the Lord.”
Heb “journey.”

verses.zh: 百姓却在所当灭的物中，取了最好的牛羊，要在吉甲献与耶和华―你的　神。」
verses.en: But the army took from the plunder some of the sheep and cattle—the best of what was to be slaughtered—to sacrifice to the Lord your God in Gilgal.”

verses.zh: 撒母耳说：耶和华喜悦燔祭和平安祭，岂如喜悦人听从他的话呢？听命胜于献祭；顺从胜于公羊的脂油。
verses.en: Then Samuel said, “Does the Lord take pleasure in burnt offerings and sacrificesas much as he does in obedience?[NOTE:1] Certainly,[NOTE:2] obedience[NOTE:3] is better than sacrifice;paying attention is better than[NOTE:4] the fat of rams.
notes: Heb “as [in] listening to the voice of the Lord.”
Heb “look.”
Heb “listening.”
The expression “is better” is understood here by ellipsis (see the immediately preceding statement).
verses.commentary:
15:22 This is one of the most powerful texts on the priority of motive over ritual (cf. Isa. 1:10-15;
Amos 5:21-24; Hos. 6:6; Matt. 9:13; 12:7; Mark 12:33). This is not meant to depreciate the sacrificial system.
It was God's will on how sinful people can approach a holy God and stay in fellowship with Him. But it was not an
automatic ritual, rather a new heart, mind (i.e., Ezek. 36:22-36), and will that showed one to be in fellowship with God (i.e., a good
example is circumcision, cf. Deut. 10:16; 30:6; Jer. 4:4; 6:10; Rom. 2:28-29).

Ritual and liturgy are effective only when accompanied by

- a believing heart

- a godly life (Micah 6:6-8)

- obedience to the known will of God (cf. Jer. 6:16-20; 7:21-26)

For a good brief discussion of this issue see Hard Sayings of the Bible, "Does the Lord
Delight in Sacrifices?" pp. 207-208, 274-275.

verses.zh: 悖逆的罪与行邪术的罪相等；顽梗的罪与拜虚神和偶像的罪相同。你既厌弃耶和华的命令，耶和华也厌弃你作王。
verses.en: For rebellion is like the sin of divination,and presumption is like the evil of idolatry.Because you have rejected the Lord’s orders,[NOTE:1]he has rejected you from being king.”
notes: Or “message, word.”
verses.commentary:
15:23 Seeking guidance and knowledge from any source but YHWH is sin/rebellion. Also to seek His will
then violate it is far worse sin!

SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINER

▣ "idolatry" This is literally "teraphim" (BDB 1076).

For a good brief discussion of divination and idolatry, see Robert Girdlestone, Synonyms of the OT,
pp. 296-311.

SPECIAL TOPIC: Teraphim

verses.zh: 扫罗对撒母耳说：「我有罪了，我因惧怕百姓，听从他们的话，就违背了耶和华的命令和你的言语。
verses.en: Then Saul said to Samuel, “I have sinned, for I have disobeyed what the Lord commanded[NOTE:1] and your words as well. For I was afraid of the army,[NOTE:2] and I obeyed their voice.
notes: Heb “the mouth of the Lord.”
Heb “people.”
verses.commentary:
15:24-25 Verbal repentance did not change Saul's heart or actions. He rejected YHWH's word; YHWH rejected
him. There are consequences to disobedience!

verses.zh: 现在求你赦免我的罪，同我回去，我好敬拜耶和华。」
verses.en: Now please forgive my sin. Go back with me so I can worship the Lord.”
verses.commentary:
15:25 Saul does seemingly repent but it was too late. YHWH had rejected him on this occasion of his second
act of disobedience. And there will be more to come! God knows the heart, but hearts change!

verses.zh: 撒母耳对扫罗说：「我不同你回去；因为你厌弃耶和华的命令，耶和华也厌弃你作以色列的王。」
verses.en: Samuel said to Saul, “I will not go back with you, for you have rejected the Lord’s orders,[NOTE:1] and the Lord has rejected you from being king over Israel!”
notes: Or “message, word.”

verses.zh: 撒母耳转身要走，扫罗就扯住他外袍的衣襟，衣襟就撕断了。
verses.en: When Samuel turned to leave, Saul[NOTE:1] grabbed the edge of his robe and it tore.
notes: Heb “he,” but Saul is clearly the referent. A Qumran ms and the LXX include the name “Saul” here.
verses.commentary:
15:27-28 This is an example of an Eastern visualized proverb.

The IVP Bible Background Commentary (OT), p. 304, asserts that this gesture of grabbing
the robe was a plea for mercy common in Ugaritic myths (i.e., Anat and Mot).

verses.zh: 撒母耳对他说：「如此，今日耶和华使以色列国与你断绝，将这国赐与比你更好的人。
verses.en: Samuel said to him, “The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel from you this day and has given it to one of your colleagues who is better than you!
verses.commentary:
15:28

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NJB, LXX, Peshitta
"neighbor"

TEV
"someone"

REB, JPSOA
"another"

NET
"one of your colleagues"

The MASCULINE NOUN (BDB 945 II, KB 1253 II) suggests "your fellow"

verses.zh: 以色列的大能者必不致说谎，也不致后悔；因为他迥非世人，决不后悔。」
verses.en: The Preeminent One[NOTE:1] of Israel does not go back on his word[NOTE:2] or change his mind, for he is not a human being who changes his mind.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “splendor,” used here by metonymy as a title for the Lord.
Or perhaps “does not lie.”

This observation marks the preceding statement (v. 28) as an unconditional, unalterable decree. When God makes such a decree he will not alter it or change his mind. This does not mean that God never deviates from his stated intentions or changes his mind. On the contrary, several passages describe him as changing his mind. In fact, his willingness to do so is one of his fundamental divine attributes (see Joel 2:13; Jonah 4:2). For a fuller discussion see R. B. Chisholm, Jr., “Does God Change His Mind?” BSac 152 (1995): 387-99.
verses.commentary:
15:29-30 Although YHWH had rejected Saul as king, the new king had not been revealed and anointed.
There must be some continuity in Israel's government. This is what Saul is asking Samuel to supply.

verses.zh: 撒母耳说：「要把亚玛力王亚甲带到我这里来。」亚甲就欢欢喜喜地来到他面前，心里说，死亡的苦难必定过去了。
verses.en: Then Samuel said, “Bring me King Agag of the Amalekites.” So Agag came to him trembling,[NOTE:1] thinking to himself,[NOTE:2] “Surely death is bitter!”[NOTE:3]
notes: The MT reading מַעֲדַנֹּת (maʿadannot, literally, “bonds,” used here adverbially, “in bonds”) is difficult. The word is found only here and in Job 38:31. Part of the problem lies in determining the root of the word. Some scholars have taken it to be from the root עָנַד (ʿanad, “to bind around”), but this assumes a metathesis of two of the letters of the root. Others take it from the root עָדַן (ʿadan) with the meaning “voluptuously,” but this does not seem to fit the context. It seems better to understand the word to be from the root מעד (maʿad, “to totter” or “shake”). In that case it describes the fear that Agag experienced in realizing the mortal danger that he faced as he approached Samuel. This is the way that the LXX translators understood the word, rendering it by the Greek participle τρέμον (tremon, “trembling”).
Heb “and Agag said.”

The text is difficult here. With the LXX, two Old Latin mss, and the Syriac Peshitta it is probably preferable to delete סָר (sar, “is past”) of the MT; it looks suspiciously like a dittograph of the following word מַר (mar, “bitter”). This further affects the interpretation of Agag’s comment. In the MT he comes to Samuel confidently assured that the danger is over (cf. KJV, NASB, NIV “Surely the bitterness of death is past,” along with NLT, CEV). However, it seems more likely that Agag realized that his fortunes had suddenly taken a turn for the worse and that the clemency he had enjoyed from Saul would not be his lot from Samuel. The present translation thus understands Agag to approach not confidently but in the stark realization that his death is imminent (“Surely death is bitter!”). Cf. NAB “So it is bitter death!”; NRSV “Surely this is the bitterness of death”; TEV “What a bitter thing it is to die!”

verses.zh: 撒母耳说：「你既用刀使妇人丧子，这样，你母亲在妇人中也必丧子。」于是，撒母耳在吉甲耶和华面前将亚甲杀死。
verses.en: Samuel said, “Just as your sword left women childless, so your mother will be the most bereaved[NOTE:1] among women.” Then Samuel hacked Agag to pieces there in Gilgal before the Lord.
notes: Heb “bereaved more than [other] women.” The verb שָׁכָל (shakal) is a stative verb in the Qal stem meaning “to be bereaved” (HALOT 1492), that is, to be deprived of a loved one (a child) by death. Stative verbs are typically modified by מִן (min) with its comparative sense. A passive verb can also behave this way; compare Judges 5:24 where Jael is “most blessed of women.” While any woman’s loss of a child is tragic, perhaps from a social perspective because of his high position as king, his mother’s loss is construed as greater.
verses.commentary:
15:33 Agag's past ruthless attacks on Israel's population deserved the judgment of God. Samuel carried out
that judgment publicly before the eyes of the Judge of the universe, the Creator of all things!
